mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or if the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within a month signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity improve.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases & UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods with increasing RSAFS, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
